claims: NASA is targeting April 1, 2026, for the launch of the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts on a 10-day test flight around the moon.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket was returned to Launch Complex-39B in late March 2026 following delays.
Daily two-hour launch windows are available between April 1 and April 6, 2026.
The target launch date for the Artemis II mission is April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT (22:24 UTC).
The launch vehicle for the Artemis II mission is Space Launch System (SLS) Rocket.
The launch location for the Artemis II mission is Kennedy Space Center, Launch Complex 39B.
The Artemis II mission type is crewed lunar flyby (no landing).
The crew for the Artemis II mission is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The duration of the Artemis II mission is 10 days, according to Space Center Houston.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the moon since 1972.
The Artemis II mission serves as a critical step before the Artemis III crewed lunar landing.
